ads_ratio.reason: EDGAR diluted share counts are in ordinary shares while the Nasdaq/NYSE price is per ADS; each ADS represents one-half of one ordinary share, so per-share figures must be scaled x0.5 ordinary shares per ADS to be comparable to the ADS price.
ads_ratio.source: Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-04-29, accession 0001193125-26-190113), cover page: 'American depositary shares, each representing one-half of share of common stock'; Item 9.A Share Capital repeats: 'One ADS represents one-half of one share of our common stock.'

moat_against: No pricing power: tariffs are set politically and the fuel-cost adjustment is capped — for Q4 2026 the formula indicated KRW 7.30/kWh and the charge was frozen at the KRW 5.00 ceiling for the 18th consecutive quarter (search results)

Measured returns through a cycle are value-destructive: fundamentals.json roic_proxy 22.73% (2015) collapsed to -47.01% (2022) and -6.36% (2023) before recovering to 9.78% (2024); gross margin was -43.0% in 2022 and -2.5% in 2023
The state is the controlling holder and uses KEPCO as a price-stabilization policy tool — the 2021-2023 tariff freeze through the fuel spike is what produced the crisis losses in the base window
Heavy leverage funds the grid build: engine net debt $12,427,953,360 with a further $2,515,630,080 of lease liabilities, and consolidated liabilities of KRW 210.7 trillion at H1 2026 (search results)
moat_for: Sole nationwide transmission and distribution operator for South Korea, with generation concentrated in its genco subsidiaries and KHNP (nuclear) — an exclusive, essential-service national franchise
Captive demand: effectively every Korean household, business and factory buys delivered power through KEPCO; share count has been flat at 641,964,077 for a decade — no dilution
Scale and state backing: FY2024 revenue $62,953,220,200 (engine, FX-converted) and continued access to bond funding through the crisis years despite the losses
moat_justification: Exclusive national T&D franchise with captive essential-service demand and generation scale, but the regulator/government — also the controlling holder — sets tariffs politically and froze them through the 2021-2023 fuel spike, so the franchise has no pricing power and its measured ROIC through the cycle is deeply negative (roic_proxy -47.01% in 2022, -6.36% in 2023, 9.78% in 2024). A durable monopoly whose economics are capped and periodically confiscated is a weak moat, not a wide one.
name: Korea Electric Power Corporation
one_liner: South Korea's state-controlled electric monopoly, moat 4/10 — Tier F on this screen: the normalized (median FY2022-24) conservative OE base is -$7.43/ADS because the window carries the tariff-freeze crisis years (OE positive in only 2 of the last 5 years), so no IV@15% or hurdle-clearing price is computable; the latest engine year (FY2024, +$0.88/ADS) and the filed FY2025 recovery show a profitable utility underneath, but on the v5 method there is no positive normalized OE stream to clear 15% with.

sbc_override.ack_reason: Out-of-band by construction: the engine has no filed SBC value for KEPCO in any period (last_filed_value is null), so any override flags out-of-band. The value is not an estimate — it is the filer's own reported position (no equity compensation plans at all; see source).
sbc_override.reason: DATA_GAP:sbc — SBC missing for fiscal years 2022, 2023, 2024 of the last 3 under every tag the engine reads. KEPCO has no equity-settled share-based payment expense to subtract: it has no equity compensation plans, so there is no equity SBC cost inside or outside operating cash flow. The filing-sourced figure for equity SBC in the gap years is 0 (same treatment as SQM, TS and LTM in this sweep).
sbc_override.source: Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-04-29, accession 0001193125-26-190113), Item 16G / NYSE-standards comparison, 'Shareholder Approval of Equity Compensation Plans': 'We currently do not have any equity compensation plans.' The term 'share-based' appears nowhere in the 20-F, and EDGAR companyfacts carries no ifrs-full AdjustmentsForSharebasedPayments / ExpenseFromSharebasedPaymentTransactionsWithEmployees (or us-gaap ShareBasedCompensation) fact for this filer in any year.
